title: API Inspector Training on the Gulf Coast: TX, LA, MS and AL
description: Self-paced online API 510, 570, 580 and 653 exam prep for Gulf Coast inspectors, with instructor Q&A. Refineries, terminals, LNG and local damage mechanisms.
h1: API Inspector Training on the Gulf Coast: Exam Prep for Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Alabama Inspectors
html:
API inspector training for the Gulf Coast refining corridor

From Corpus Christi Bay to the Mississippi River parishes, the Gulf Coast holds the densest concentration of refineries, chemical plants, tank terminals and export docks in the United States. It is also where most US API inspectors learn the job. This page is for inspectors, NDT technicians, welders, operators and engineers in Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi and coastal Alabama who are preparing for API 510, API 570, API 580 or API 653.

Atlantis has an office in Houston, but there is no Atlantis classroom anywhere on the Gulf Coast. The exam-prep courses are self-paced online courses with instructor Q&A, so a candidate in Port Arthur studies exactly the same material as one in Pascagoula. The American Petroleum Institute sets eligibility, administers each examination in person at Prometric test centres and issues the certification. Atlantis is not an API-approved training provider.

Where API inspectors work along the Gulf Coast

EIA's refinery capacity survey for the start of 2026 lists 34 refineries in Texas with about 6.1 million barrels per calendar day of crude distillation capacity and 15 in Louisiana with about 3.0 million. Together that is roughly half of the 18.2 million barrels per calendar day operating nationally. Motiva's Port Arthur refinery is the largest in the country on a calendar-day basis and Marathon's Galveston Bay refinery in Texas City the largest on a stream-day basis. Mississippi's capacity is dominated by Chevron at Pascagoula, and Alabama's largest refinery is Vertex Refining at Saraland, just north of Mobile.

The map does change. LyondellBasell's Houston refinery stopped operating in March 2025, yet EIA reports that Gulf Coast refining capacity fell by less than 2% during 2025, while new LNG trains kept starting up along the coast.

Tank farms, export docks and LNG: where 653 and 510 meet

Refineries are only half the story. Enbridge describes its Ingleside Energy Center on Corpus Christi Bay as the largest crude storage and export facility by volume in the United States, with about 20 million barrels of storage after its latest tank expansion. A Houston port region economic profile describes the area as the largest petrochemical manufacturing complex in the country, with connections to more than 400 million barrels of storage across the nearby ports. Every one of those atmospheric tanks needs inspections, repair approvals and settlement evaluations that an API 653 inspector is trained for.

Pipeline companies add another layer. Under 49 CFR 195.432, operators of hazardous liquid pipelines must inspect their atmospheric and low-pressure steel breakout tanks according to API Std 653, and that rule does not allow the risk-based procedures in API 653 to set the internal inspection interval. Tank farms that feed the Gulf's long-haul crude and product lines therefore employ 653 inspectors whether or not they sit beside a refinery.

LNG terminals are a different case. DOE's LNG export snapshot lists Sabine Pass, Cameron, Calcasieu Pass and Plaquemines in Louisiana and Corpus Christi, Freeport and Golden Pass in Texas as operating, with more under construction at Port Arthur, Brownsville and in Cameron and Calcasieu parishes. Their large refrigerated LNG storage tanks are built to other standards and sit outside API 653's scope. The process side of each terminal, with its pre-treatment vessels, exchangers and piping, is where API 510 and API 570 inspectors find work once the plant is in service. Pressurised LPG spheres and bullets at fractionation and export sites are pressure vessels too, so they fall to API 510 rather than API 653.

Which API certifications Gulf Coast employers ask for

The equipment decides the certificate, and the Gulf has all of it in one place, which is why many inspectors here end up holding two or three API cards.

  • Refinery and chemical plant inspection groups lean on API 510 and API 570, because a process unit is a network of vessels joined by piping. A unit inspector who holds both can cover a whole unit at turnaround.
  • Terminal and pipeline operators look for API 653, sometimes with API 570 for the dock and manifold piping that connects tanks to ships and pipelines.
  • Reliability and RBI teams at the larger refineries add API 580, and often API 571 for corrosion and materials, once their inspectors move into planning and programme work.
  • Inspection contractors staffing spring and autumn turnarounds value inspectors who hold more than one code, because a single person can be moved between vessel, piping and tank scopes as the work changes.

New construction is not API 510, 570 or 653 work: those are in-service codes. Inspectors on the LNG and chemical projects now being built along the coast usually work to construction codes, often with AWS CWI or ASNT NDT credentials, and move into API roles once the plant starts up. Atlantis runs the AWS CWI exam prep in Houston and ASNT NDT training across the Gulf Coast for those earlier steps.

Damage mechanisms Gulf Coast inspectors meet every week

Humid, salty coastal air and a high water table shape the corrosion picture here, and the exam's damage-mechanism questions read differently once you have seen them in the field.

  • Corrosion under insulation. Wet insulation on carbon steel lines and vessels is a constant concern in a climate with frequent rain and high humidity. API RP 583 is the industry reference; the CUI glossary entry and the API RP 583 explainer summarise it.
  • External chloride stress corrosion cracking. Austenitic stainless steel under wet insulation can crack when chlorides from the marine atmosphere or the insulation itself concentrate on a warm surface.
  • Atmospheric and splash-zone corrosion. Dock piping, pipe supports and tank shells near the water corrode faster than the same equipment inland, so CML placement at supports and soil-to-air interfaces matters.
  • Wet H2S damage. Sour water, amine and overhead systems can suffer hydrogen blistering, hydrogen-induced cracking, SOHIC and sulfide stress cracking, all covered in API RP 571.
  • Tank bottom and soil-side corrosion. Coastal soils and groundwater put tank bottoms at risk from below, which is why cathodic protection under API RP 651 and internal linings under API RP 652 typically appear in the 653 Body of Knowledge.

Weather adds its own inspection work. After a major storm or flood, owners typically check tanks for shell damage, floating-roof problems and foundation washout, and check piping supports and insulation for water ingress before restart. Knowing which code paragraphs govern a repair or an evaluation in those conditions is exactly the open-book skill the exam rewards. Damage-mechanism reviews for whole sites are covered on the damage mechanism review page.

State and federal rules on Gulf Coast work

For process equipment, the main driver is federal. OSHA's Process Safety Management standard makes covered plants inspect and test their process equipment according to recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices, and API 510, API 570 and API 653 are the practices Gulf Coast refiners and chemical producers commonly name in their mechanical integrity programmes.

State programmes mostly concern boilers. In Texas, the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation registers and inspects boilers, and its published summary of the boiler program lists power boilers, heating boilers, unfired steam boilers and process steam generators, not unfired process vessels. In Louisiana, the Office of State Fire Marshal administers the state boiler law. For the columns, drums and exchangers that make up a refinery unit, the inspection programme is therefore usually the owner's own, and the owner decides which certifications its inspectors and contractors must hold. Always confirm the requirement with the site before you assume a certificate covers a scope.

Pipeline tank farms fall under PHMSA's rules described above. Owners who need NDE and data review rather than training can see the state pages for API 510 vessel inspection support in Texas, API 570 piping inspection support in Louisiana and API 653 tank inspection support in Texas.

Studying around turnarounds, shifts and storm season

A self-paced course fits Gulf Coast working patterns better than a fixed class, because the patterns are rarely regular. Inspectors on rotating 12-hour shifts study on their days off; contractors on a turnaround may work six or seven long days a week for the length of the job and study almost nothing until it ends. Plan backwards from the exam window: pick the window first, mark the turnarounds you are likely to be booked on, and put the heaviest reading in the months between them.

  • Avoid sitting the exam straight after a turnaround. Fatigue costs more marks on the open-book half than on any other part of the day.
  • Allow for storm season. The Atlantic hurricane season runs from the start of June to the end of November. A storm can close roads, delay a test appointment or call you back to site, so keep some slack in your plan if your window falls in late summer.
  • Use the instructor when the field and the code disagree. Gulf Coast inspectors often know a site practice that differs from the code text the exam tests. Send that question; the answer from the code is the one that scores.

Prometric lists test centres in and around the larger Gulf Coast cities. You choose one in Prometric's locator when you book, with API's acceptance of your application in hand.

Routes into API certification for Gulf Coast workers

The coast has more people with relevant experience than almost anywhere, but API still checks the experience against the equipment of the code you apply for. Typical starting points look like this:

  • UT technicians who have run thickness surveys and corrosion monitoring on refinery piping circuits, often with an ASNT Level II, usually have the clearest path to API 570. NDT training for those roles is described on the Houston, Beaumont, Corpus Christi, Lake Charles and Baton Rouge NDT training pages.
  • Welders and welding inspectors from fabrication shops and repair crews can count repair and fabrication experience, and many take the CWI step first.
  • Operators with years on a unit bring operating experience; the one year of supervising or performing inspection is the part they usually need to build.
  • Engineers from the large owner-users reach API 510 or API 570 eligibility after one year of inspection activity with a bachelor's degree.
  • Veterans with technical military service can use it in place of part of the education requirement, unless the discharge was dishonorable.

The education and experience scale is set out in full on the API 510, API 570 and API 653 certification pages. API 580 is automatic for anyone holding a current 510, 570 or 653.

Gulf Coast employers sponsoring API candidates

Owner-users and contractors along the coast often sponsor several candidates at once, ahead of a busy turnaround year or when a site needs more certified inspectors for a new unit. A sponsored group can include different exams, so a contractor might prepare two technicians for API 570 and a tank lead for API 653 in the same enquiry. Fees are quoted on request. Each candidate applies to API individually, studies at their own pace and asks the instructor their own questions. Employers help most by signing accurate experience records and by keeping the exam window clear of the candidate's turnaround assignments.

faq.q: Can I take API exam prep in a Houston classroom?
faq.a: Not from Atlantis. Atlantis has an office in Houston, but there is no Atlantis classroom in Houston or anywhere else on the Gulf Coast. The API 510, 570, 580 and 653 exam-prep courses are self-paced online courses with instructor Q&A, which suits rotating shifts and turnaround travel. You sit the examination itself at a Prometric test centre after API approves your application.

faq.q: Which API certification is most useful on the Gulf Coast?
faq.a: It depends on the equipment you work on. Refinery and chemical plant inspection groups rely on API 510 and API 570, terminal and pipeline operators on API 653, and RBI teams add API 580. Many Gulf Coast inspectors hold two codes because contractors can then move them between vessel and piping scopes during a turnaround. Start with the code that matches the experience you can document.

faq.q: Does Texas require a state licence to work as an API inspector?
faq.a: API certification on Texas refinery, chemical and terminal work is normally a requirement of the owner's inspection programme rather than a state licence. The state boiler program, run by the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation, registers and inspects boilers; its published summary does not list unfired process vessels. Requirements differ by site and scope, so confirm them with the owner or contractor before you rely on any certificate.

faq.q: Do LNG terminal jobs on the Gulf Coast need API 653?
faq.a: Usually not for the main LNG storage tanks, which are refrigerated tanks built to other standards and outside API 653's scope. The process side of an LNG terminal, with pre-treatment vessels, exchangers and piping, needs API 510 and API 570 inspectors once it is in service. Tank farms and terminals storing crude, products and chemicals at atmospheric pressure are where API 653 work concentrates.

faq.q: Can I study for API 570 while working a turnaround?
faq.a: You can, but most candidates find it hard to study much during long turnaround shifts. Because the course is self-paced, you can slow down during the job and pick up the reading again when it ends, and the instructor answers questions whenever you send them. Choose an exam window that does not fall straight after a turnaround, since fatigue costs marks on the open-book half of the day.

faq.q: Where do Gulf Coast candidates sit the API exam?
faq.a: At a Prometric test centre. Prometric lists test centres in and around the larger Gulf Coast cities, and you choose one when you book your appointment after API accepts your application. The examination is computer-based; for the open-book part of API 510, 570 and 653 the code documents are on the screen, and you may not bring your own books or notes.

faq.q: Can a Gulf Coast contractor sponsor a group of inspectors?
faq.a: Yes. A contractor or owner-user can enrol several candidates, including candidates preparing for different API exams, and fees are quoted on request. Each candidate applies to API individually with their own documented experience. Tell us the exams, the windows you are aiming at and the number of candidates when you enquire, and plan the windows around your turnaround calendar.
